args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001.

1. **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
2. **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. I didn't need change-manager approval because v2.3.0 had been healthy before. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback, and the next step: finding the root cause before v2.3.1 is redeployed. The request to create it came back with a server error, so I checked the incident list before trying again. It had already been created, so there's only one incident and no duplicate page.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
